questions.stem: A model is needed only to describe the overall three-dimensional arrangement of electron domains in NH3; it need not describe the detailed orbital overlap. Choose between VSEPR and a hybrid-orbital overlap diagram, and identify what your chosen model predicts and what it leaves unresolved.
conditions: Introductory valence-bond model and VSEPR rules apply; assume ideal coordination geometry unless specified.

answer.summary: Chosen model: VSEPR. What it predicts: overall 3D electron-domain arrangement (tetrahedral) and molecular geometry (trigonal pyramidal) with angle compression (~107°) by minimizing electrostatic repulsion. What it leaves unresolved: wave-mechanical nature of bonds, atomic orbital mixing, orbital symmetry/phases, bond energies, and electronic spectroscopy.

answer.check: VSEPR successfully predicts tetrahedral domain arrangement and ~107° trigonal pyramidal geometry without invoking orbital overlap.

questions.stem: For a qualitative orbital sketch, overlap A is end-on along the internuclear axis and overlap B is side-on on opposite sides of that axis. Classify each as sigma or pi overlap and identify the defining feature you used.
conditions: Introductory valence-bond model and VSEPR rules apply; assume ideal coordination geometry unless specified.

answer.summary: Overlap A is a sigma (σ) overlap; defining feature is end-on (head-to-head) coaxial overlap along the internuclear axis, possessing cylindrical symmetry with maximum electron density along the axis. Overlap B is a pi (π) overlap; defining feature is lateral (side-on) overlap of parallel orbitals, possessing a nodal plane passing through the internuclear axis.

reasoning_route.why_valid: The internuclear axis serves as the spatial reference connecting the two nuclei.
End-on coaxial overlap produces cylindrical symmetry along the axis with maximum density between nuclei.
Lateral side-on overlap of parallel orbitals creates a nodal plane containing the internuclear axis.
Sigma has non-zero density along the axis; pi has zero density (nodal plane) on the axis.

answer.check: A = sigma (coaxial, cylindrical); B = pi (parallel, nodal plane on axis).

scaffolds.text: Look at the orientation of overlapping lobes relative to the internuclear axis.
Identify which overlap is coaxial and symmetric about the bond axis.
Classify end-on as sigma and side-on as pi, stating the nodal/symmetry feature that distinguishes them.

difficulty.basis: Overlap A is end-on along internuclear axis; Overlap B is side-on on opposite sides of internuclear axis. Decisive move: Classify A as sigma and B as pi, and provide the defining symmetry/nodal criteria.. Total score 3 -> D2.

conditions: Introductory valence-bond model and VSEPR rules apply; assume ideal coordination geometry unless specified.

questions.stem: A student counts the double bond in H2C=O as two separate directions and predicts four domains around carbon. Locate the counting error and give the corrected domain count.
conditions: Introductory valence-bond model and VSEPR rules apply; assume ideal coordination geometry unless specified.

Corrected count: 2 (C-H bonds) + 1 (C=O bond) = 3 electron domains around carbon (trigonal planar, sp2).
